paras: The attack on the "Our Kids" troupe at Home City, Kansas, was an assault in March 1903 by white townspeople on members of a touring company of six Black vaudeville performers, followed by its rejection by hotels at Marysville. Threatened with being followed, the performers cancelled their next date and were turned away by four Marysville hotels. The Topeka State Journal ran the story as "This Was in Kansas," and the Savannah Morning News used it to taunt Kansans about Black "rights."

According to the troupe's leader, after a Saturday-night show at Home City, about March 14, "some of the white boys of the town" attacked some members, asserting they were "girls in male attire." No injuries were described. When the attackers threatened to follow them to Beattie, the performers cancelled their Monday date there.

On Sunday the six arrived at Marysville on the westbound train in "gaudy uniforms," and a crowd gathered. Their leader said they were not stopping, and a bystander answered, "We haven't got any use for your class of people." Four hotels refused them, and on Monday they left for an engagement at Oketo. The leader told a reporter that Kansas was "a hard old state on the black man" and that the troupe would leave it as soon as it could.
No report of arrests or official action appears in the coverage.

The story ran in two white papers, and no Black-press account appears in the coverage. The Topeka State Journal's Marysville dispatch of March 18 remarked that local citizens "do not seem to like negroes" but called the troupe "the aggregation" and printed its leader's words in dialect. Two days later the Savannah Morning News retold it editorially, noting that Kansans demanded Black "rights"—"in Mississippi!"

The Savannah paper called the attackers "a mob of white men" and said Marysville would not let the players stop "even long enough to get a bite to eat." The Marysville dispatch, the closer source, said only that hotels refused them and that it was not known where they ate.

reader.title: Attack on the "Our Kids" troupe at Home City, Kansas
bases: The violence reported is a physical attack by white townspeople on several members of a Black troupe at Home City, followed by a threat to follow them and by refusal of lodging in Marysville; no one was ordered out of Marysville by force (A1, A2, A3).
Both Topeka items are one Marysville dispatch (A1, A2), and the Savannah editorial (A3) retells the same story without a separate dateline or new witnesses, so the episode rests on one report.

accounts.label: Marysville correspondent, relaying the troupe leader
accounts.gist: White boys of Home City attacked some members after the show, claiming they were girls in male attire, and threatened to follow them to Beattie; at Marysville the troupe was refused at four hotels and left Monday for Oketo.

accounts.label: Savannah editorial
accounts.gist: A mob of white men attacked the six performers and warned them they would be 'roughly handled' at the next town; Marysville would not let them stop even to eat.

framing.detail: Topeka's 'This Was in Kansas' reports the snub with some irony at Marysville's expense but calls the troupe 'the aggregation' and its leader the leader 'of the gang,' and prints his words in dialect.
Savannah retells the attack to taunt Kansas, 'the state of "Osawatomie John Brown,"' for demanding Black 'rights' only 'in Mississippi!'
